segments.text: Hello my friends.
segments.ipa: /həˈloʊ maɪ frɛndz/

segments.text: Welcome back to English Unleashed. I'm Tom.
segments.ipa: /ˈwɛlkəm bæk tu ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ənˈliʃt aɪm tɑm/

segments.text: In today's episode, I will talk about a useful self-growth book called The Mountain is You.
segments.ipa: /ɪn təˈdeɪz ˈɛpəˌsoʊd aɪ wɪl tɔk əˈbaʊt ə ˈjusfəl self-growth bʊk kɔld ðə ˈmaʊntən ɪz ju/

segments.text: The author is Brianna Wiest.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈɔθər ɪz briˈænə ˈwaɪɪst/

segments.text: As always, I will speak slowly and naturally.
segments.ipa: /æz ˈɔlˌweɪz aɪ wɪl spik ˈsloʊli ənd ˈnætʃərəli/

segments.text: I will use simple words and easy grammar, so you understand everything.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɪl jus ˈsɪmpəl wɝdz ənd ˈizi ˈɡræmər soʊ ju ˌʌndərˈstænd ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ/

segments.text: This book is about self-sabotage.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs bʊk ɪz əˈbaʊt self-sabotage/

segments.text: Self-sabotage means you do things that stop your own progress.
segments.ipa: /Self-sabotage minz ju du θɪŋz ðæt stɑp jɔr oʊn ˈprɑˌɡrɛs/

segments.text: You want something good, but you also do something that makes it harder.
segments.ipa: /ju wɑnt ˈsʌmθɪŋ ɡʊd bʌt ju ˈɔlsoʊ du ˈsʌmθɪŋ ðæt meɪks ɪt ˈhɑrdər/

segments.text: You want to change, but you keep going back to old habits.
segments.ipa: /ju wɑnt tu tʃeɪndʒ bʌt ju kip ˈɡoʊɪŋ bæk tu oʊld ˈhæbəts/

segments.text: You want peace, but you keep choosing stress.
segments.ipa: /ju wɑnt pis bʌt ju kip ˈtʃuzɪŋ strɛs/

segments.text: You want confidence, but you keep speaking to yourself in a negative way.
segments.ipa: /ju wɑnt ˈkɑnfədəns bʌt ju kip ˈspikɪŋ tu jərˈsɛlf ɪn ə ˈnɛɡətɪv weɪ/

segments.text: This, my friends, is a very human problem.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs maɪ frɛndz ɪz ə ˈvɛri ˈhjumən ˈprɑbləm/

segments.text: Many people experience it.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈpipəl ɪkˈspɪriəns ɪt/

segments.text: Maybe you want to wake up early, but you sleep late again.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju wɑnt tu weɪk ʌp ˈɝli bʌt ju slip leɪt əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: Maybe you want to learn English, but you keep delaying your practice.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju wɑnt tu lɝn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ bʌt ju kip dɪˈleɪɪŋ jɔr ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: Maybe you want to be healthier, but you keep eating in a way that makes you feel bad.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju wɑnt tu bi ˈhɛlθiər bʌt ju kip ˈitɪŋ ɪn ə weɪ ðæt meɪks ju fil bæd/

segments.text: Maybe you want a better life, but you keep returning to people, places, or habits that hurt you.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju wɑnt ə ˈbɛtər laɪf bʌt ju kip rɪˈtɝnɪŋ tu ˈpipəl ˈpleɪsəz ɔr ˈhæbəts ðæt hɝt ju/

segments.text: The book uses a strong image, the mountain.
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk ˈjusəz ə strɔŋ ˈɪmədʒ ðə ˈmaʊntən/

segments.text: A mountain is big.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈmaʊntən ɪz bɪɡ/

segments.text: A mountain is difficult to climb.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈmaʊntən ɪz ˈdɪfəkəlt tu klaɪm/

segments.text: A mountain stands in front of you.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈmaʊntən stændz ɪn frʌnt ʌv ju/

segments.text: It can feel impossible.
segments.ipa: /ɪt kæn fil ˌɪmˈpɑsəbəl/

segments.text: But in this book, the mountain is not only outside you.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪn ðɪs bʊk ðə ˈmaʊntən ɪz nɑt ˈoʊnli ˈaʊtˈsaɪd ju/

segments.text: The mountain is inside you.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈmaʊntən ɪz ˌɪnˈsaɪd ju/

segments.text: Mountain is your fear.
segments.ipa: /ˈmaʊntən ɪz jɔr fɪr/

segments.text: The mountain is your old pain.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈmaʊntən ɪz jɔr oʊld peɪn/

segments.text: The mountain is your self-doubt.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈmaʊntən ɪz jɔr self-doubt/

segments.text: The mountain is your bad habits.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈmaʊntən ɪz jɔr bæd ˈhæbəts/

segments.text: The mountain is the part of you that wants change, but is also afraid of change.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈmaʊntən ɪz ðə pɑrt ʌv ju ðæt wɑnts tʃeɪndʒ bʌt ɪz ˈɔlsoʊ əˈfreɪd ʌv tʃeɪndʒ/

segments.text: This idea is very important.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs aɪˈdiə ɪz ˈvɛri ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt/

segments.text: Sometimes we think the problem is only outside.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz wi θɪŋk ðə ˈprɑbləm ɪz ˈoʊnli ˈaʊtˈsaɪd/

segments.text: We say, "My life is difficult because of other people."
segments.ipa: /wi seɪ maɪ laɪf ɪz ˈdɪfəkəlt bɪˈkɔz ʌv ˈʌðər ˈpipəl/

segments.text: Or I cannot change because of my situation.
segments.ipa: /ɔr aɪ ˈkænɑt tʃeɪndʒ bɪˈkɔz ʌv maɪ ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən/

segments.text: Or I cannot move forward because the world is against me.
segments.ipa: /ɔr aɪ ˈkænɑt muv ˈfɔrwərd bɪˈkɔz ðə wɝld ɪz əˈɡɛnst mi/

segments.text: Of course, outside problems are real.
segments.ipa: /ʌv kɔrs ˈaʊtˈsaɪd ˈprɑbləmz ɑr ril/

segments.text: Life can be really hard.
segments.ipa: /laɪf kæn bi ˈrɪli hɑrd/

segments.text: People can hurt us.
segments.ipa: /ˈpipəl kæn hɝt ʌs/

segments.text: Money can be difficult.
segments.ipa: /ˈmʌni kæn bi ˈdɪfəkəlt/

segments.text: Work can be stressful.
segments.ipa: /wɝk kæn bi ˈstrɛsfəl/

segments.text: Family can be complicated.
segments.ipa: /ˈfæməli kæn bi ˈkɑmpləˌkeɪtəd/

segments.text: But this book asks us to look inside, too.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðɪs bʊk æsks ʌs tu lʊk ˌɪnˈsaɪd tu/

segments.text: It asks, "What am I doing again and again that keeps me stuck?
segments.ipa: /ɪt æsks wʌt æm aɪ ˈduɪŋ əˈɡɛn ənd əˈɡɛn ðæt kips mi stʌk/

segments.text: What am I avoiding?
segments.ipa: /wʌt æm aɪ əˈvɔɪdɪŋ/

segments.text: What am I afraid to feel?
segments.ipa: /wʌt æm aɪ əˈfreɪd tu fil/

segments.text: What old story am I telling myself?"
segments.ipa: /wʌt oʊld ˈstɔri æm aɪ ˈtɛlɪŋ ˌmaɪˈsɛlf/

segments.text: This is not about blaming yourself.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz nɑt əˈbaʊt ˈbleɪmɪŋ jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: Blaming yourself is not useful.
segments.ipa: /ˈbleɪmɪŋ jərˈsɛlf ɪz nɑt ˈjusfəl/

segments.text: The goal is not to say, "Everything is my fault." No.
segments.ipa: /ðə ɡoʊl ɪz nɑt tu seɪ ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ ɪz maɪ fɔlt noʊ/

segments.text: The goal is to understand yourself.
segments.ipa: /ðə ɡoʊl ɪz tu ˌʌndərˈstænd jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: Understanding is different from blame.
segments.ipa: /ˌʌndərˈstændɪŋ ɪz ˈdɪfərənt frʌm bleɪm/

segments.text: Blame makes you feel small.
segments.ipa: /bleɪm meɪks ju fil smɔl/

segments.text: Understanding helps you grow.
segments.ipa: /ˌʌndərˈstændɪŋ hɛlps ju ɡroʊ/

segments.text: The book says that self-sabotage is often a sign of an unmet need.
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk sɛz ðæt self-sabotage ɪz ˈɔfən ə saɪn ʌv æn ənˈmɛt nid/

segments.text: This means there is something inside you that needs attention.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs minz ðɛr ɪz ˈsʌmθɪŋ ˌɪnˈsaɪd ju ðæt nidz əˈtɛnʃən/

segments.text: Maybe you keep delaying work because you are afraid of failure.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju kip dɪˈleɪɪŋ wɝk bɪˈkɔz ju ɑr əˈfreɪd ʌv ˈfeɪljər/

segments.text: Maybe you keep choosing the wrong people because you are afraid of being alone.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju kip ˈtʃuzɪŋ ðə rɔŋ ˈpipəl bɪˈkɔz ju ɑr əˈfreɪd ʌv ˈbiɪŋ əˈloʊn/

segments.text: Maybe you keep working too much because you are afraid of feeling empty.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju kip ˈwɝkɪŋ tu mʌtʃ bɪˈkɔz ju ɑr əˈfreɪd ʌv ˈfilɪŋ ˈɛmpti/

segments.text: Maybe you keep avoiding success because success feels unfamiliar.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju kip əˈvɔɪdɪŋ səkˈsɛs bɪˈkɔz səkˈsɛs filz ˌʌnfəˈmɪljər/

segments.text: These are unmet needs.
segments.ipa: /ðiz ɑr ənˈmɛt nidz/

segments.text: Needs that you have not paid attention to.
segments.ipa: /nidz ðæt ju hæv nɑt peɪd əˈtɛnʃən tu/

segments.text: This is a deep idea.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ə dip aɪˈdiə/

segments.text: Sometimes good things feel uncomfortable because we are not used to them.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz ɡʊd θɪŋz fil ənˈkʌmfərtəbəl bɪˈkɔz wi ɑr nɑt juzd tu ðɛm/

segments.text: Peace can feel strange if you have lived with a stress for a long time.
segments.ipa: /pis kæn fil streɪndʒ ɪf ju hæv lɪvd wɪð ə strɛs fɔr ə lɔŋ taɪm/

segments.text: Healthy love can feel strange if you are used to drama.
segments.ipa: /ˈhɛlθi lʌv kæn fil streɪndʒ ɪf ju ɑr juzd tu ˈdrɑmə/

segments.text: Success can feel strange if you are used to struggling.
segments.ipa: /səkˈsɛs kæn fil streɪndʒ ɪf ju ɑr juzd tu ˈstrʌɡəlɪŋ/

segments.text: Calm can feel strange if your body is used to worry.
segments.ipa: /kɑm kæn fil streɪndʒ ɪf jɔr ˈbɑdi ɪz juzd tu ˈwɝi/

segments.text: So, change is not only about getting something new.
segments.ipa: /soʊ tʃeɪndʒ ɪz nɑt ˈoʊnli əˈbaʊt ˈɡɛtɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ nu/

segments.text: Change is also about becoming comfortable with a new version of yourself.
segments.ipa: /tʃeɪndʒ ɪz ˈɔlsoʊ əˈbaʊt bɪˈkʌmɪŋ ˈkʌmfərtəbəl wɪð ə nu ˈvɝʒən ʌv jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: For English learners, this is very useful.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnərz ðɪs ɪz ˈvɛri ˈjusfəl/

segments.text: Maybe you say, "I want to speak English fluently."
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju seɪ aɪ wɑnt tu spik ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈfluəntli/

segments.text: But when you have a chance to speak, you avoid it. Why?
segments.ipa: /bʌt wɛn ju hæv ə tʃæns tu spik ju əˈvɔɪd ɪt waɪ/

segments.text: Maybe because speaking makes you feel exposed.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi bɪˈkɔz ˈspikɪŋ meɪks ju fil ɪkˈspoʊzd/

segments.text: Exposed means people can see your mistakes.
segments.ipa: /ɪkˈspoʊzd minz ˈpipəl kæn si jɔr mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: Maybe you are afraid someone will judge you.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju ɑr əˈfreɪd ˈsʌmˌwʌn wɪl dʒʌdʒ ju/

segments.text: Maybe you are afraid your English will not be perfect.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju ɑr əˈfreɪd jɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ wɪl nɑt bi pərˈfɛkt/

segments.text: So, you avoid speaking and then you feel bad because you are not improving.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ju əˈvɔɪd ˈspikɪŋ ənd ðɛn ju fil bæd bɪˈkɔz ju ɑr nɑt ˌɪmˈpruvɪŋ/

segments.text: This is self-sabotage.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz self-sabotage/

segments.text: You want progress, but fear stops you from doing the thing that creates progress.
segments.ipa: /ju wɑnt ˈprɑˌɡrɛs bʌt fɪr stɑps ju frʌm ˈduɪŋ ðə θɪŋ ðæt kriˈeɪts ˈprɑˌɡrɛs/

segments.text: The solution is not to hate yourself.
segments.ipa: /ðə səˈluʃən ɪz nɑt tu heɪt jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: The solution is to notice the pattern gently.
segments.ipa: /ðə səˈluʃən ɪz tu ˈnoʊtəs ðə ˈpætərn ˈdʒɛntli/

segments.text: You can say, "I'm avoiding speaking because I feel afraid.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn seɪ aɪm əˈvɔɪdɪŋ ˈspikɪŋ bɪˈkɔz aɪ fil əˈfreɪd/

segments.text: This fear is trying to protect me, but I can take one small step."
segments.ipa: /ðɪs fɪr ɪz ˈtraɪɪŋ tu prəˈtɛkt mi bʌt aɪ kæn teɪk wʌn smɔl stɛp/

segments.text: This is a kind way to grow.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ə kaɪnd weɪ tu ɡroʊ/

segments.text: You do not attack yourself.
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt əˈtæk jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: You guide yourself.
segments.ipa: /ju ɡaɪd jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: The book reminds us that the mountain is not here to destroy us.
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk riˈmaɪndz ʌs ðæt ðə ˈmaʊntən ɪz nɑt hir tu dɪˈstrɔɪ ʌs/

segments.text: The mountain is here to show us where we need to grow.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈmaʊntən ɪz hir tu ʃoʊ ʌs wɛr wi nid tu ɡroʊ/

segments.text: The problem we keep facing may be the doorway to our growth.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈprɑbləm wi kip ˈfeɪsɪŋ meɪ bi ðə ˈdɔrˌweɪ tu ˈaʊər ɡroʊθ/

segments.text: The fear we keep avoiding may be the place where our strength is waiting.
segments.ipa: /ðə fɪr wi kip əˈvɔɪdɪŋ meɪ bi ðə pleɪs wɛr ˈaʊər strɛŋkθ ɪz ˈweɪtɪŋ/

segments.text: This does not mean pain is good.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs dʌz nɑt min peɪn ɪz ɡʊd/

segments.text: Pain can be very hard, but pain can teach us something if we listen carefully.
segments.ipa: /peɪn kæn bi ˈvɛri hɑrd bʌt peɪn kæn titʃ ʌs ˈsʌmθɪŋ ɪf wi ˈlɪsən ˈkɛrfəli/

segments.text: It can show us what needs healing.
segments.ipa: /ɪt kæn ʃoʊ ʌs wʌt nidz ˈhilɪŋ/

segments.text: It can show us what needs changing.
segments.ipa: /ɪt kæn ʃoʊ ʌs wʌt nidz ˈtʃeɪndʒɪŋ/

segments.text: It can show us what we cannot ignore anymore.
segments.ipa: /ɪt kæn ʃoʊ ʌs wʌt wi ˈkænɑt ˌɪɡˈnɔr ˌɛniˈmɔr/

segments.text: Many people wait for life to change before they change themselves.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈpipəl weɪt fɔr laɪf tu tʃeɪndʒ bɪˈfɔr ðeɪ tʃeɪndʒ ðɛmˈsɛlvz/

segments.text: They say, "When things become easier, I will become better."
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ seɪ wɛn θɪŋz bɪˈkʌm ˈiziər aɪ wɪl bɪˈkʌm ˈbɛtər/

segments.text: But often, life changes when we begin to change our response.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈɔfən laɪf ˈtʃeɪndʒəz wɛn wi bɪˈɡɪn tu tʃeɪndʒ ˈaʊər rɪˈspɑns/

segments.text: We cannot control everything, but we can control small daily choices.
segments.ipa: /wi ˈkænɑt kənˈtroʊl ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ bʌt wi kæn kənˈtroʊl smɔl ˈdeɪli ˈtʃɔɪsəz/

segments.text: We can control how we speak to ourselves.
segments.ipa: /wi kæn kənˈtroʊl haʊ wi spik tu aʊərˈsɛlvz/

segments.text: We can control what we practice.
segments.ipa: /wi kæn kənˈtroʊl wʌt wi ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: We can control what we repeat.
segments.ipa: /wi kæn kənˈtroʊl wʌt wi rɪˈpit/

segments.text: We can control whether we take one small step or stay in the same place.
segments.ipa: /wi kæn kənˈtroʊl ˈwɛðər wi teɪk wʌn smɔl stɛp ɔr steɪ ɪn ðə seɪm pleɪs/

segments.text: So, the mountain is not climbed in one day.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ðə ˈmaʊntən ɪz nɑt klaɪmd ɪn wʌn deɪ/

segments.text: This is important.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt/

segments.text: You do not wake up one morning and become a completely new person.
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt weɪk ʌp wʌn ˈmɔrnɪŋ ənd bɪˈkʌm ə kəmˈplitli nu ˈpɝsən/

segments.text: You climb slowly.
segments.ipa: /ju klaɪm ˈsloʊli/

segments.text: One step, then another step, then another step.
segments.ipa: /wʌn stɛp ðɛn əˈnʌðər stɛp ðɛn əˈnʌðər stɛp/

segments.text: Some days you move forward.
segments.ipa: /sʌm deɪz ju muv ˈfɔrwərd/

segments.text: Some days you feel tired.
segments.ipa: /sʌm deɪz ju fil ˈtaɪərd/

segments.text: Some days you slip back.
segments.ipa: /sʌm deɪz ju slɪp bæk/

segments.text: That is normal.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz ˈnɔrməl/

segments.text: Growth is not a straight line.
segments.ipa: /ɡroʊθ ɪz nɑt ə streɪt laɪn/

segments.text: Growth is messy.
segments.ipa: /ɡroʊθ ɪz ˈmɛsi/

segments.text: But messy progress is still progress.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈmɛsi ˈprɑˌɡrɛs ɪz stɪl ˈprɑˌɡrɛs/

segments.text: So, in this episode, we will talk about self-sabotage, emotions, fear, healing, habits, identity,
segments.ipa: /soʊ ɪn ðɪs ˈɛpəˌsoʊd wi wɪl tɔk əˈbaʊt self-sabotage ɪˈmoʊʃənz fɪr ˈhilɪŋ ˈhæbəts aɪˈdɛntɪˌti/

segments.text: and becoming your future self.
segments.ipa: /ənd bɪˈkʌmɪŋ jɔr ˈfjutʃər sɛlf/

segments.text: So, for now, remember this first lesson.
segments.ipa: /soʊ fɔr naʊ rɪˈmɛmbər ðɪs fɝst ˈlɛsən/

segments.text: The mountain is not only the problem in front of you.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈmaʊntən ɪz nɑt ˈoʊnli ðə ˈprɑbləm ɪn frʌnt ʌv ju/

segments.text: The mountain is also the pattern inside you.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈmaʊntən ɪz ˈɔlsoʊ ðə ˈpætərn ˌɪnˈsaɪd ju/

segments.text: And when you understand the pattern, you can begin to change it. Okay.
segments.ipa: /ənd wɛn ju ˌʌndərˈstænd ðə ˈpætərn ju kæn bɪˈɡɪn tu tʃeɪndʒ ɪt ˌoʊˈkeɪ/

segments.text: Now, let's go deeper into the idea of self-sabotage.
segments.ipa: /naʊ lɛts ɡoʊ ˈdipər ˈɪntu ðə aɪˈdiə ʌv self-sabotage/

segments.text: Self-sabotage can sound strange.
segments.ipa: /Self-sabotage kæn saʊnd streɪndʒ/

segments.text: Why would we stop ourselves?
segments.ipa: /waɪ wʊd wi stɑp aʊərˈsɛlvz/

segments.text: Why would we hurt our own progress?
segments.ipa: /waɪ wʊd wi hɝt ˈaʊər oʊn ˈprɑˌɡrɛs/

segments.text: Why would we do things that make life harder?
segments.ipa: /waɪ wʊd wi du θɪŋz ðæt meɪk laɪf ˈhɑrdər/

segments.text: Most people do not wake up and say, "Today, I want to ruin my life." No.
segments.ipa: /moʊst ˈpipəl du nɑt weɪk ʌp ənd seɪ təˈdeɪ aɪ wɑnt tu ˈruən maɪ laɪf noʊ/

segments.text: Self-sabotage is usually not conscious.
segments.ipa: /Self-sabotage ɪz ˈjuʒəwəli nɑt ˈkɑnʃəs/

segments.text: Conscious means you know you are doing it.
segments.ipa: /ˈkɑnʃəs minz ju noʊ ju ɑr ˈduɪŋ ɪt/

segments.text: Many times, self-sabotage is unconscious.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni taɪmz self-sabotage ɪz ˌʌnˈkɑnʃəs/

segments.text: It happens quietly.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ˈhæpənz ˈkwaɪətli/

segments.text: It happens through habits, emotions, excuses, fear, and old beliefs.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ˈhæpənz θru ˈhæbəts ɪˈmoʊʃənz ɪkskˈjusɪz fɪr ənd oʊld bɪˈlifs/

segments.text: You may want change, but another part of you wants safety.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ wɑnt tʃeɪndʒ bʌt əˈnʌðər pɑrt ʌv ju wɑnts ˈseɪfti/

segments.text: This is one of the main ideas in the book.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz wʌn ʌv ðə meɪn aɪˈdiəz ɪn ðə bʊk/

segments.text: Your mind likes what feels familiar.
segments.ipa: /jɔr maɪnd laɪks wʌt filz fəˈmɪljər/

segments.text: Familiar means known.
segments.ipa: /fəˈmɪljər minz noʊn/

segments.text: It means usual.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz ˈjuʒəwəl/

segments.text: It means something that you have experienced many times before.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz ˈsʌmθɪŋ ðæt ju hæv ɪkˈspɪriənst ˈmɛni taɪmz bɪˈfɔr/

segments.text: Even if something is not good for you, it may still feel familiar.
segments.ipa: /ˈivɪn ɪf ˈsʌmθɪŋ ɪz nɑt ɡʊd fɔr ju ɪt meɪ stɪl fil fəˈmɪljər/

segments.text: And because it feels familiar, your brain may choose it again.
segments.ipa: /ənd bɪˈkɔz ɪt filz fəˈmɪljər jɔr breɪn meɪ tʃuz ɪt əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: This is why people sometimes return to bad habits.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz waɪ ˈpipəl səmˈtaɪmz rɪˈtɝn tu bæd ˈhæbəts/

segments.text: The bad habit is not healthy, but it is known.
segments.ipa: /ðə bæd ˈhæbət ɪz nɑt ˈhɛlθi bʌt ɪt ɪz noʊn/

segments.text: It feels safe in a strange way.
segments.ipa: /ɪt filz seɪf ɪn ə streɪndʒ weɪ/

segments.text: Change may be better, but change is unknown.
segments.ipa: /tʃeɪndʒ meɪ bi ˈbɛtər bʌt tʃeɪndʒ ɪz ənˈnoʊn/

segments.text: It is unfamiliar, and the unknown can feel scary.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ˌʌnfəˈmɪljər ənd ðə ənˈnoʊn kæn fil ˈskɛri/

segments.text: For example, imagine someone who always feels stressed.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ˌɪˈmædʒən ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu ˈɔlˌweɪz filz strɛst/

segments.text: They say, "I want peace."
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ seɪ aɪ wɑnt pis/

segments.text: But when life becomes peaceful, they feel uncomfortable.
segments.ipa: /bʌt wɛn laɪf bɪˈkʌmz ˈpisfəl ðeɪ fil ənˈkʌmfərtəbəl/

segments.text: They start looking for problems.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ stɑrt ˈlʊkɪŋ fɔr ˈprɑbləmz/

segments.text: They start overthinking.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ stɑrt overthinking/

segments.text: They start creating drama. Why?
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ stɑrt kriˈeɪtɪŋ ˈdrɑmə waɪ/

segments.text: Because stress feels normal to their nervous system.
segments.ipa: /bɪˈkɔz strɛs filz ˈnɔrməl tu ðɛr ˈnɝvəs ˈsɪstəm/

segments.text: Peace feels unfamiliar.
segments.ipa: /pis filz ˌʌnfəˈmɪljər/

segments.text: This idea does not mean they truly want stress.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs aɪˈdiə dʌz nɑt min ðeɪ ˈtruli wɑnt strɛs/

segments.text: It means their body is used to stress.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz ðɛr ˈbɑdi ɪz juzd tu strɛs/

segments.text: Their body has learned stress as a normal state.
segments.ipa: /ðɛr ˈbɑdi hæz lɝnd strɛs æz ə ˈnɔrməl steɪt/

segments.text: So now, they need to learn peace slowly.
segments.ipa: /soʊ naʊ ðeɪ nid tu lɝn pis ˈsloʊli/

segments.text: This is a powerful idea.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ə ˈpaʊərfəl aɪˈdiə/

segments.text: Sometimes we do not need to force big change.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz wi du nɑt nid tu fɔrs bɪɡ tʃeɪndʒ/

segments.text: We need to teach our body and mind that good things are safe.
segments.ipa: /wi nid tu titʃ ˈaʊər ˈbɑdi ənd maɪnd ðæt ɡʊd θɪŋz ɑr seɪf/

segments.text: Calm is safe.
segments.ipa: /kɑm ɪz seɪf/

segments.text: Success is safe.
segments.ipa: /səkˈsɛs ɪz seɪf/

segments.text: Love is safe.
segments.ipa: /lʌv ɪz seɪf/

segments.text: Visibility is safe.
segments.ipa: /ˌvɪzəˈbɪlɪti ɪz seɪf/

segments.text: Speaking English with the mistakes is safe.
segments.ipa: /ˈspikɪŋ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ wɪð ðə mɪˈsteɪks ɪz seɪf/

segments.text: Trying something new is safe.
segments.ipa: /ˈtraɪɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ nu ɪz seɪf/

segments.text: For English learners, self-sabotage may look like this.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnərz self-sabotage meɪ lʊk laɪk ðɪs/

segments.text: You buy books, watch videos, and make plans, but you do not practice speaking.
segments.ipa: /ju baɪ bʊks wɑtʃ ˈvɪdioʊz ənd meɪk plænz bʌt ju du nɑt ˈpræktəs ˈspikɪŋ/

segments.text: You keep preparing, but you do not act.
segments.ipa: /ju kip priˈpɛrɪŋ bʌt ju du nɑt ækt/

segments.text: You tell yourself, "I will speak when I'm ready."
segments.ipa: /ju tɛl jərˈsɛlf aɪ wɪl spik wɛn aɪm ˈrɛdi/

segments.text: But, the truth is, speaking is how you become ready.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðə truθ ɪz ˈspikɪŋ ɪz haʊ ju bɪˈkʌm ˈrɛdi/

segments.text: You cannot become confident only by waiting.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈkænɑt bɪˈkʌm ˈkɑnfədənt ˈoʊnli baɪ ˈweɪtɪŋ/

segments.text: Confidence grows through action.
segments.ipa: /ˈkɑnfədəns ɡroʊz θru ˈækʃən/

segments.text: Here is another example.
segments.ipa: /hir ɪz əˈnʌðər ɪɡˈzæmpəl/

segments.text: You want to improve listening, but you keep choosing materials that are too difficult.
segments.ipa: /ju wɑnt tu ˌɪmˈpruv ˈlɪsənɪŋ bʌt ju kip ˈtʃuzɪŋ məˈtɪriəlz ðæt ɑr tu ˈdɪfəkəlt/

segments.text: Then, you feel frustrated.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ju fil ˈfrʌˌstreɪtəd/

segments.text: You say, "I cannot understand English."
segments.ipa: /ju seɪ aɪ ˈkænɑt ˌʌndərˈstænd ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: But, maybe the problem is not your ability.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈmeɪbi ðə ˈprɑbləm ɪz nɑt jɔr əˈbɪləˌti/

segments.text: Maybe the material is too hard.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðə məˈtɪriəl ɪz tu hɑrd/

segments.text: A kinder choice would be simple, clear, repeated listening.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈkaɪndər tʃɔɪs wʊd bi ˈsɪmpəl klɪr rɪˈpitɪd ˈlɪsənɪŋ/

segments.text: But, sometimes we choose difficulty because we think learning must feel painful.
segments.ipa: /bʌt səmˈtaɪmz wi tʃuz ˈdɪfəkəlti bɪˈkɔz wi θɪŋk ˈlɝnɪŋ mʌst fil ˈpeɪnfəl/

segments.text: That can become another kind of self-sabotage.
segments.ipa: /ðæt kæn bɪˈkʌm əˈnʌðər kaɪnd ʌv self-sabotage/

segments.text: The book helps us ask an important question.
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk hɛlps ʌs æsk æn ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt ˈkwɛstʃən/

segments.text: "What is this behavior doing for me?"
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɪz ðɪs bɪˈheɪvjər ˈduɪŋ fɔr mi/

segments.text: This question may sound strange.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ˈkwɛstʃən meɪ saʊnd streɪndʒ/

segments.text: If the behavior is bad, how can it do something for me?
segments.ipa: /ɪf ðə bɪˈheɪvjər ɪz bæd haʊ kæn ɪt du ˈsʌmθɪŋ fɔr mi/

segments.text: But, many bad habits give us something in the short term.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈmɛni bæd ˈhæbəts ɡɪv ʌs ˈsʌmθɪŋ ɪn ðə ʃɔrt tɝm/

segments.text: Maybe they give comfort.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ ɡɪv ˈkʌmfərt/

segments.text: Maybe they help us avoid fear.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ hɛlp ʌs əˈvɔɪd fɪr/

segments.text: Maybe they help us escape responsibility.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ hɛlp ʌs ɪˈskeɪp riˌspɑnsəˈbɪləti/

segments.text: Maybe they help us avoid rejection.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ hɛlp ʌs əˈvɔɪd rɪˈdʒɛkʃən/

segments.text: For example, procrastination means delaying something. Procrastination.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl prəˌkræstəˈneɪʃən minz dɪˈleɪɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ prəˌkræstəˈneɪʃən/

segments.text: That's a big word.
segments.ipa: /ðæts ə bɪɡ wɝd/

segments.text: You have work to do, but you do not start.
segments.ipa: /ju hæv wɝk tu du bʌt ju du nɑt stɑrt/

segments.text: Procrastination looks like laziness, but often it is fear.
segments.ipa: /prəˌkræstəˈneɪʃən lʊks laɪk ˈleɪzinəs bʌt ˈɔfən ɪt ɪz fɪr/

segments.text: If you do not start, you cannot fail.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju du nɑt stɑrt ju ˈkænɑt feɪl/

segments.text: If you do not finish, nobody can judge your final work.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju du nɑt ˈfɪnɪʃ ˈnoʊˌbɑˌdi kæn dʒʌdʒ jɔr ˈfaɪnəl wɝk/

segments.text: If you keep delaying, you stay in a safe middle place.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju kip dɪˈleɪɪŋ ju steɪ ɪn ə seɪf ˈmɪdəl pleɪs/

segments.text: You're not successful, but you are also not fully exposed.
segments.ipa: /jʊr nɑt səkˈsɛsfəl bʌt ju ɑr ˈɔlsoʊ nɑt ˈfʊli ɪkˈspoʊzd/

segments.text: So, procrastination protects you from fear, but it also keeps you stuck.
segments.ipa: /soʊ prəˌkræstəˈneɪʃən prəˈtɛkts ju frʌm fɪr bʌt ɪt ˈɔlsoʊ kips ju stʌk/

segments.text: This is why self-sabotage is complicated.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz waɪ self-sabotage ɪz ˈkɑmpləˌkeɪtəd/

segments.text: It often tries to protect us, but in the wrong way.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ˈɔfən traɪz tu prəˈtɛkt ʌs bʌt ɪn ðə rɔŋ weɪ/

segments.text: Protects us from discomfort, but it also blocks growth.
segments.ipa: /prəˈtɛkts ʌs frʌm dɪˈskʌmfərt bʌt ɪt ˈɔlsoʊ blɑks ɡroʊθ/

segments.text: It protects us from short-term pain, but it creates long-term pain.
segments.ipa: /ɪt prəˈtɛkts ʌs frʌm ˌʃɔrtˈtɝm peɪn bʌt ɪt kriˈeɪts ˈlɔŋˈtɝm peɪn/

segments.text: So, let's say that again because it is very important.
segments.ipa: /soʊ lɛts seɪ ðæt əˈɡɛn bɪˈkɔz ɪt ɪz ˈvɛri ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt/

segments.text: Self-sabotage protects us from short-term discomfort, but it creates long-term problems.
segments.ipa: /Self-sabotage prəˈtɛkts ʌs frʌm ˌʃɔrtˈtɝm dɪˈskʌmfərt bʌt ɪt kriˈeɪts ˈlɔŋˈtɝm ˈprɑbləmz/

segments.text: If you avoid speaking English today, you feel safe today.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju əˈvɔɪd ˈspikɪŋ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ təˈdeɪ ju fil seɪf təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: But later, you still cannot speak confidently.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈleɪtər ju stɪl ˈkænɑt spik ˈkɑnfədəntli/

segments.text: If you avoid difficult conversations today, you feel safe today.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju əˈvɔɪd ˈdɪfəkəlt ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃənz təˈdeɪ ju fil seɪf təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: But later, the relationship may become worse.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈleɪtər ðə riˈleɪʃənˌʃɪp meɪ bɪˈkʌm wɝs/

segments.text: If you avoid starting your project today, you feel safe today.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju əˈvɔɪd ˈstɑrtɪŋ jɔr ˈprɑdʒɛkt təˈdeɪ ju fil seɪf təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: But later, your dream is still only a dream.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈleɪtər jɔr drim ɪz stɪl ˈoʊnli ə drim/

segments.text: So, the question becomes, am I choosing short-term comfort or long-term growth?
segments.ipa: /soʊ ðə ˈkwɛstʃən bɪˈkʌmz æm aɪ ˈtʃuzɪŋ ˌʃɔrtˈtɝm ˈkʌmfərt ɔr ˈlɔŋˈtɝm ɡroʊθ/

segments.text: Growth often requires discomfort, not extreme pain, not suffering, but discomfort.
segments.ipa: /ɡroʊθ ˈɔfən riˈkwaɪərz dɪˈskʌmfərt nɑt ɛkˈstrim peɪn nɑt ˈsʌfərɪŋ bʌt dɪˈskʌmfərt/

segments.text: You may feel nervous.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ fil ˈnɝvəs/

segments.text: You may feel unsure.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ fil ənˈʃʊr/

segments.text: You may feel like a beginner.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ fil laɪk ə bɪˈɡɪnər/

segments.text: You may feel slow.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ fil sloʊ/

segments.text: That is okay.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz ˌoʊˈkeɪ/

segments.text: These feelings do not mean you should stop.
segments.ipa: /ðiz ˈfilɪŋz du nɑt min ju ʃʊd stɑp/

segments.text: They mean you are entering a new area.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ min ju ɑr ˈɛntərɪŋ ə nu ˈɛriə/

segments.text: The book also teaches that we need to stop fighting ourselves and start understanding ourselves.
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk ˈɔlsoʊ ˈtitʃəz ðæt wi nid tu stɑp ˈfaɪtɪŋ aʊərˈsɛlvz ənd stɑrt ˌʌndərˈstændɪŋ aʊərˈsɛlvz/

segments.text: If you keep saying, "I'm lazy. I'm hopeless."
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju kip ˈseɪɪŋ aɪm ˈleɪzi aɪm ˈhoʊpləs/

segments.text: You make change harder.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪk tʃeɪndʒ ˈhɑrdər/

segments.text: Negative self-talk creates more shame.
segments.ipa: /ˈnɛɡətɪv self-talk kriˈeɪts mɔr ʃeɪm/

segments.text: Shame makes people hide.
segments.ipa: /ʃeɪm meɪks ˈpipəl haɪd/

segments.text: And hiding creates more self-sabotage.
segments.ipa: /ənd ˈhaɪdɪŋ kriˈeɪts mɔr self-sabotage/

segments.text: A better way is curiosity.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈbɛtər weɪ ɪz ˌkjʊriˈɑsəti/

segments.text: Curiosity means asking questions with an open mind.
segments.ipa: /ˌkjʊriˈɑsəti minz ˈæskɪŋ ˈkwɛstʃənz wɪð æn ˈoʊpən maɪnd/

segments.text: Instead of saying, "Why am I so lazy?"
segments.ipa: /ˌɪnˈstɛd ʌv ˈseɪɪŋ waɪ æm aɪ soʊ ˈleɪzi/

segments.text: say, "What am I afraid of?"
segments.ipa: /seɪ wʌt æm aɪ əˈfreɪd ʌv/

segments.text: Instead of saying, "Why do I always ruin things?"
segments.ipa: /ˌɪnˈstɛd ʌv ˈseɪɪŋ waɪ du aɪ ˈɔlˌweɪz ˈruən θɪŋz/

segments.text: say, "What need am I trying to meet?"
segments.ipa: /seɪ wʌt nid æm aɪ ˈtraɪɪŋ tu mit/

segments.text: Instead of saying, "I am broken."
segments.ipa: /ˌɪnˈstɛd ʌv ˈseɪɪŋ aɪ æm ˈbroʊkən/

segments.text: say, "What pattern am I repeating?"
segments.ipa: /seɪ wʌt ˈpætərn æm aɪ rɪˈpitɪŋ/

segments.text: This language matters.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ˈlæŋɡwədʒ ˈmætərz/

segments.text: The way you talk to yourself becomes the way you treat yourself.
segments.ipa: /ðə weɪ ju tɔk tu jərˈsɛlf bɪˈkʌmz ðə weɪ ju trit jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: If you speak to yourself like an enemy, growth becomes painful.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju spik tu jərˈsɛlf laɪk æn ˈɛnəmi ɡroʊθ bɪˈkʌmz ˈpeɪnfəl/

segments.text: If you speak to yourself like a guide, growth becomes possible.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju spik tu jərˈsɛlf laɪk ə ɡaɪd ɡroʊθ bɪˈkʌmz ˈpɑsəbəl/

segments.text: For English practice, you can say, "I avoided speaking today because I felt nervous.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈpræktəs ju kæn seɪ aɪ əˈvɔɪdɪd ˈspikɪŋ təˈdeɪ bɪˈkɔz aɪ fɛlt ˈnɝvəs/

segments.text: Tomorrow, I will speak for just 1 minute."
segments.ipa: /təˈmɑˌroʊ aɪ wɪl spik fɔr dʒʌst ˈmɪnət/

segments.text: I did not understand the podcast the first time, so I will listen again more slowly.
segments.ipa: /aɪ dɪd nɑt ˌʌndərˈstænd ðə ˈpɔdˌkæst ðə fɝst taɪm soʊ aɪ wɪl ˈlɪsən əˈɡɛn mɔr ˈsloʊli/

segments.text: I made mistakes, but mistakes are part of learning.
segments.ipa: /aɪ meɪd mɪˈsteɪks bʌt mɪˈsteɪks ɑr pɑrt ʌv ˈlɝnɪŋ/

segments.text: This is gentle.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈdʒɛntəl/

segments.text: This is realistic.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˌriəˈlɪstɪk/

segments.text: This helps you continue.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs hɛlps ju kənˈtɪnju/

segments.text: So, the lesson of this part is this.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ðə ˈlɛsən ʌv ðɪs pɑrt ɪz ðɪs/

segments.text: We sabotage ourselves because part of us is trying to stay safe.
segments.ipa: /wi ˈsæbəˌtɑʒ aʊərˈsɛlvz bɪˈkɔz pɑrt ʌv ʌs ɪz ˈtraɪɪŋ tu steɪ seɪf/

segments.text: But safety is not always growth.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈseɪfti ɪz nɑt ˈɔlˌweɪz ɡroʊθ/

segments.text: Sometimes the old safe place becomes a prison.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz ðə oʊld seɪf pleɪs bɪˈkʌmz ə ˈprɪzən/

segments.text: A prison is a place where you cannot move freely.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈprɪzən ɪz ə pleɪs wɛr ju ˈkænɑt muv ˈfrili/

segments.text: To grow, we need to understand the old pattern, thank it for trying to protect us,
segments.ipa: /tu ɡroʊ wi nid tu ˌʌndərˈstænd ðə oʊld ˈpætərn θæŋk ɪt fɔr ˈtraɪɪŋ tu prəˈtɛkt ʌs/

segments.text: and then choose a new response.
segments.ipa: /ənd ðɛn tʃuz ə nu rɪˈspɑns/

segments.text: You are not your self-sabotage.
segments.ipa: /ju ɑr nɑt jɔr self-sabotage/

segments.text: You are the person who can notice it, understand it, and slowly change it.
segments.ipa: /ju ɑr ðə ˈpɝsən hu kæn ˈnoʊtəs ɪt ˌʌndərˈstænd ɪt ənd ˈsloʊli tʃeɪndʒ ɪt/

segments.text: In this book, emotions are very important.
segments.ipa: /ɪn ðɪs bʊk ɪˈmoʊʃənz ɑr ˈvɛri ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt/

segments.text: The book teaches us that feelings are not enemies.
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk ˈtitʃəz ʌs ðæt ˈfilɪŋz ɑr nɑt ˈɛnəmiz/

segments.text: Feelings are messengers.
segments.ipa: /ˈfilɪŋz ɑr ˈmɛsəndʒərz/

segments.text: A messenger brings a message.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈmɛsəndʒər brɪŋz ə ˈmɛsədʒ/

segments.text: So, when you feel something strong, maybe anger, sadness, fear, jealousy, or anxiety, the feeling may be trying to show you something.
segments.ipa: /soʊ wɛn ju fil ˈsʌmθɪŋ strɔŋ ˈmeɪbi ˈæŋɡər ˈsædnəs fɪr ˈdʒɛləsi ɔr æŋˈzaɪəti ðə ˈfilɪŋ meɪ bi ˈtraɪɪŋ tu ʃoʊ ju ˈsʌmθɪŋ/

segments.text: Many people do not know how to deal with feelings.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈpipəl du nɑt noʊ haʊ tu dil wɪð ˈfilɪŋz/

segments.text: Some people ignore them.
segments.ipa: /sʌm ˈpipəl ˌɪɡˈnɔr ðɛm/

segments.text: Some people hide them.
segments.ipa: /sʌm ˈpipəl haɪd ðɛm/

segments.text: Some people push them down.
segments.ipa: /sʌm ˈpipəl pʊʃ ðɛm daʊn/

segments.text: Some people become controlled by them.
segments.ipa: /sʌm ˈpipəl bɪˈkʌm kənˈtroʊld baɪ ðɛm/

segments.text: But the book suggests a different way.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðə bʊk səˈdʒɛsts ə ˈdɪfərənt weɪ/

segments.text: Feel the emotion.
segments.ipa: /fil ðə ɪˈmoʊʃən/

segments.text: Listen to it.
segments.ipa: /ˈlɪsən tu ɪt/

segments.text: Ask what it is trying to tell you.
segments.ipa: /æsk wʌt ɪt ɪz ˈtraɪɪŋ tu tɛl ju/

segments.text: This does not mean every feeling is correct.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs dʌz nɑt min ˈɛvəri ˈfilɪŋ ɪz kərˈɛkt/

segments.text: Feelings are real, but they're not always facts.
segments.ipa: /ˈfilɪŋz ɑr ril bʌt ðɛr nɑt ˈɔlˌweɪz fækts/

segments.text: This is important.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt/

segments.text: If you feel afraid, the fear is real, but it does not always mean you are in danger.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju fil əˈfreɪd ðə fɪr ɪz ril bʌt ɪt dʌz nɑt ˈɔlˌweɪz min ju ɑr ɪn ˈdeɪndʒər/

segments.text: If you feel rejected, the feeling is real, but it does not always mean people hate you.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju fil rɪˈdʒɛktɪd ðə ˈfilɪŋ ɪz ril bʌt ɪt dʌz nɑt ˈɔlˌweɪz min ˈpipəl heɪt ju/

segments.text: If you feel like a failure, the feeling is real, but it does not mean you are a failure.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju fil laɪk ə ˈfeɪljər ðə ˈfilɪŋ ɪz ril bʌt ɪt dʌz nɑt min ju ɑr ə ˈfeɪljər/

segments.text: Feelings are information.
segments.ipa: /ˈfilɪŋz ɑr ˌɪnfərˈmeɪʃən/

segments.text: They are not always instructions.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ ɑr nɑt ˈɔlˌweɪz ˌɪnˈstrʌkʃənz/

segments.text: For example, you feel nervous before speaking English.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ju fil ˈnɝvəs bɪˈfɔr ˈspikɪŋ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: This feeling gives you information.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ˈfilɪŋ ɡɪvz ju ˌɪnfərˈmeɪʃən/

segments.text: It says, "This matters to me."
segments.ipa: /ɪt sɛz ðɪs ˈmætərz tu mi/

segments.text: It says, "I want to do well."
segments.ipa: /ɪt sɛz aɪ wɑnt tu du wɛl/

segments.text: It may also say, "I am afraid of being judged."
segments.ipa: /ɪt meɪ ˈɔlsoʊ seɪ aɪ æm əˈfreɪd ʌv ˈbiɪŋ dʒʌdʒd/

segments.text: But the feeling does not have to be an instruction to run away.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðə ˈfilɪŋ dʌz nɑt hæv tu bi æn ˌɪnˈstrʌkʃən tu rʌn əˈweɪ/

segments.text: You can feel nervous and still speak.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn fil ˈnɝvəs ənd stɪl spik/

segments.text: This is a powerful skill.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ə ˈpaʊərfəl skɪl/

segments.text: You do not need to wait until fear disappears.
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt nid tu weɪt ənˈtɪl fɪr ˌdɪsəˈpɪrz/

segments.text: You can act with fear beside you.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ækt wɪð fɪr bɪˈsaɪd ju/

segments.text: You can say, "I feel nervous, but I can answer one question."
segments.ipa: /ju kæn seɪ aɪ fil ˈnɝvəs bʌt aɪ kæn ˈænsər wʌn ˈkwɛstʃən/

segments.text: You can say, "I feel unsure, but I can take one small step."
segments.ipa: /ju kæn seɪ aɪ fil ənˈʃʊr bʌt aɪ kæn teɪk wʌn smɔl stɛp/

segments.text: The book also talks about emotional avoidance.
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk ˈɔlsoʊ tɔks əˈbaʊt ɪˈmoʊʃənəl əˈvɔɪdəns/

segments.text: Avoidance means staying away from something.
segments.ipa: /əˈvɔɪdəns minz ˈsteɪɪŋ əˈweɪ frʌm ˈsʌmθɪŋ/

segments.text: Emotional avoidance means staying away from feelings.
segments.ipa: /ɪˈmoʊʃənəl əˈvɔɪdəns minz ˈsteɪɪŋ əˈweɪ frʌm ˈfilɪŋz/

segments.text: We may keep ourselves busy because we do not want to feel sadness.
segments.ipa: /wi meɪ kip aʊərˈsɛlvz ˈbɪzi bɪˈkɔz wi du nɑt wɑnt tu fil ˈsædnəs/

segments.text: We may scroll on the phone because we do not want to feel loneliness.
segments.ipa: /wi meɪ skroʊl ɑn ðə foʊn bɪˈkɔz wi du nɑt wɑnt tu fil ˈloʊnlinəs/

segments.text: We may eat too much because we do not want to feel stress.
segments.ipa: /wi meɪ it tu mʌtʃ bɪˈkɔz wi du nɑt wɑnt tu fil strɛs/

segments.text: We may work too much because we do not want to feel emptiness.
segments.ipa: /wi meɪ wɝk tu mʌtʃ bɪˈkɔz wi du nɑt wɑnt tu fil ˈɛmptinəs/

segments.text: The problem is that avoided feelings do not disappear. They wait.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈprɑbləm ɪz ðæt əˈvɔɪdɪd ˈfilɪŋz du nɑt ˌdɪsəˈpɪr ðeɪ weɪt/

segments.text: They stay in the body.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ steɪ ɪn ðə ˈbɑdi/

segments.text: They come back later, sometimes stronger.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ kʌm bæk ˈleɪtər səmˈtaɪmz ˈstrɔŋər/

segments.text: So, healing begins when we stop running away from ourselves.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ˈhilɪŋ bɪˈɡɪnz wɛn wi stɑp ˈrʌnɪŋ əˈweɪ frʌm aʊərˈsɛlvz/

segments.text: Healing means becoming whole again.
segments.ipa: /ˈhilɪŋ minz bɪˈkʌmɪŋ hoʊl əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: It means meeting the parts of ourselves that we ignored.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz ˈmitɪŋ ðə pɑrts ʌv aʊərˈsɛlvz ðæt wi ˌɪɡˈnɔrd/

segments.text: It means saying, "I am ready to listen."
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz ˈseɪɪŋ aɪ æm ˈrɛdi tu ˈlɪsən/

segments.text: Not all at once, not in a dramatic way.
segments.ipa: /nɑt ɔl æt wʌns nɑt ɪn ə drəˈmætɪk weɪ/

segments.text: Slowly, safely, and kindly.
segments.ipa: /ˈsloʊli ˈseɪfli ənd ˈkaɪndli/

segments.text: Sometimes a feeling is connected to an old story.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz ə ˈfilɪŋ ɪz kəˈnɛktɪd tu æn oʊld ˈstɔri/

segments.text: For example, you may learn as a child that mistakes are dangerous.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ju meɪ lɝn æz ə tʃaɪld ðæt mɪˈsteɪks ɑr ˈdeɪndʒərəs/

segments.text: Maybe people laughed when you make mistakes.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ˈpipəl læft wɛn ju meɪk mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: Maybe you were criticized.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju wɝ ˈkrɪtəˌsaɪzd/

segments.text: Now as an adult, you avoid trying new things because mistakes still feel dangerous.
segments.ipa: /naʊ æz æn əˈdʌlt ju əˈvɔɪd ˈtraɪɪŋ nu θɪŋz bɪˈkɔz mɪˈsteɪks stɪl fil ˈdeɪndʒərəs/

segments.text: But the present is not the past.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðə ˈprɛzənt ɪz nɑt ðə pæst/

segments.text: You can teach yourself a new story.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn titʃ jərˈsɛlf ə nu ˈstɔri/

segments.text: The old story says, "If I make a mistake, I am not good enough."
segments.ipa: /ðə oʊld ˈstɔri sɛz ɪf aɪ meɪk ə mɪˈsteɪk aɪ æm nɑt ɡʊd ɪˈnʌf/

segments.text: The new story is if I make a mistake, I am learning.
segments.ipa: /ðə nu ˈstɔri ɪz ɪf aɪ meɪk ə mɪˈsteɪk aɪ æm ˈlɝnɪŋ/

segments.text: The new story says some people may judge me, but I can still grow.
segments.ipa: /ðə nu ˈstɔri sɛz sʌm ˈpipəl meɪ dʒʌdʒ mi bʌt aɪ kæn stɪl ɡroʊ/

segments.text: The old story says I must be perfect to be accepted.
segments.ipa: /ðə oʊld ˈstɔri sɛz aɪ mʌst bi pərˈfɛkt tu bi ækˈsɛptɪd/

segments.text: The new story says I can be human and still be worthy.
segments.ipa: /ðə nu ˈstɔri sɛz aɪ kæn bi ˈhjumən ənd stɪl bi ˈwɝði/

segments.text: This is very important.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈvɛri ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt/

segments.text: Many people try to improve themselves because they hate themselves.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈpipəl traɪ tu ˌɪmˈpruv ðɛmˈsɛlvz bɪˈkɔz ðeɪ heɪt ðɛmˈsɛlvz/

segments.text: They think if I become better, then I will finally be enough.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ θɪŋk ɪf aɪ bɪˈkʌm ˈbɛtər ðɛn aɪ wɪl ˈfaɪnəli bi ɪˈnʌf/

segments.text: But the book suggests a healthier way.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðə bʊk səˈdʒɛsts ə ˈhɛlθiər weɪ/

segments.text: You are always worthy and because you are worthy, you can care for your life.
segments.ipa: /ju ɑr ˈɔlˌweɪz ˈwɝði ənd bɪˈkɔz ju ɑr ˈwɝði ju kæn kɛr fɔr jɔr laɪf/

segments.text: You can improve not because you hate yourself, but because you respect yourself.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˌɪmˈpruv nɑt bɪˈkɔz ju heɪt jərˈsɛlf bʌt bɪˈkɔz ju rɪˈspɛkt jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: You can say, "I am learning because I care about my life."
segments.ipa: /ju kæn seɪ aɪ æm ˈlɝnɪŋ bɪˈkɔz aɪ kɛr əˈbaʊt maɪ laɪf/

segments.text: This is a much kinder sentence.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ə mʌtʃ ˈkaɪndər ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: Another idea in the book is that emotions can show us where we need boundaries.
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər aɪˈdiə ɪn ðə bʊk ɪz ðæt ɪˈmoʊʃənz kæn ʃoʊ ʌs wɛr wi nid ˈbaʊndəriz/

segments.text: A boundary is a line.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈbaʊndəri ɪz ə laɪn/

segments.text: It shows what is okay and what is not okay.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ʃoʊz wʌt ɪz ˌoʊˈkeɪ ənd wʌt ɪz nɑt ˌoʊˈkeɪ/

segments.text: If you often feel tired, angry, or used by other people, maybe you need stronger boundaries.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju ˈɔfən fil ˈtaɪərd ˈæŋɡri ɔr juzd baɪ ˈʌðər ˈpipəl ˈmeɪbi ju nid ˈstrɔŋər ˈbaʊndəriz/

segments.text: Maybe you say yes too often.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju seɪ jɛs tu ˈɔfən/

segments.text: Maybe you give too much.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju ɡɪv tu mʌtʃ/

segments.text: Maybe you do not protect your time.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju du nɑt prəˈtɛkt jɔr taɪm/

segments.text: Boundaries are not walls.
segments.ipa: /ˈbaʊndəriz ɑr nɑt wɔlz/

segments.text: They are healthy lines.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ ɑr ˈhɛlθi laɪnz/

segments.text: They help relationships become clearer.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ hɛlp riˈleɪʃənˌʃɪps bɪˈkʌm ˈklɪrər/

segments.text: A boundary can sound like, "I cannot do that today.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈbaʊndəri kæn saʊnd laɪk aɪ ˈkænɑt du ðæt təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: I need some time to think.
segments.ipa: /aɪ nid sʌm taɪm tu θɪŋk/

segments.text: I am not comfortable with that.
segments.ipa: /aɪ æm nɑt ˈkʌmfərtəbəl wɪð ðæt/

segments.text: I can help, but not right now.
segments.ipa: /aɪ kæn hɛlp bʌt nɑt raɪt naʊ/

segments.text: These phrases are simple but powerful.
segments.ipa: /ðiz ˈfreɪzəz ɑr ˈsɪmpəl bʌt ˈpaʊərfəl/

segments.text: They protect your energy.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ prəˈtɛkt jɔr ˈɛnərdʒi/

segments.text: For English learners, boundaries can also mean protecting your learning time.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnərz ˈbaʊndəriz kæn ˈɔlsoʊ min prəˈtɛktɪŋ jɔr ˈlɝnɪŋ taɪm/

segments.text: If you say you want to improve, but you give all your time away,
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju seɪ ju wɑnt tu ˌɪmˈpruv bʌt ju ɡɪv ɔl jɔr taɪm əˈweɪ/

segments.text: your learning will suffer.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˈlɝnɪŋ wɪl ˈsʌfər/

segments.text: Maybe you need to say, "This 30 minutes is for English."
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju nid tu seɪ ðɪs ˈmɪnəts ɪz fɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: Not in a harsh way, but in a respectful way.
segments.ipa: /nɑt ɪn ə hɑrʃ weɪ bʌt ɪn ə rɪˈspɛktfəl weɪ/

segments.text: So, the book asks us to become more honest with ourselves.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ðə bʊk æsks ʌs tu bɪˈkʌm mɔr ˈɑnəst wɪð aʊərˈsɛlvz/

segments.text: What do I feel?
segments.ipa: /wʌt du aɪ fil/

segments.text: What do I mean?
segments.ipa: /wʌt du aɪ min/

segments.text: What am I avoiding?
segments.ipa: /wʌt æm aɪ əˈvɔɪdɪŋ/

segments.text: What am I pretending not to know?
segments.ipa: /wʌt æm aɪ priˈtɛndɪŋ nɑt tu noʊ/

segments.text: These questions are not always easy.
segments.ipa: /ðiz ˈkwɛstʃənz ɑr nɑt ˈɔlˌweɪz ˈizi/

segments.text: But they can open the door to change.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðeɪ kæn ˈoʊpən ðə dɔr tu tʃeɪndʒ/

segments.text: Remember, emotions are not bad.
segments.ipa: /rɪˈmɛmbər ɪˈmoʊʃənz ɑr nɑt bæd/

segments.text: They are human.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ ɑr ˈhjumən/

segments.text: Fear, sadness, anger, and jealousy are not signs that you are broken.
segments.ipa: /fɪr ˈsædnəs ˈæŋɡər ənd ˈdʒɛləsi ɑr nɑt saɪnz ðæt ju ɑr ˈbroʊkən/

segments.text: They are signs that something inside you wants attention.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ ɑr saɪnz ðæt ˈsʌmθɪŋ ˌɪnˈsaɪd ju wɑnts əˈtɛnʃən/

segments.text: So, when a feeling appears, pause, breathe, and ask, "What is this feeling trying to show me?
segments.ipa: /soʊ wɛn ə ˈfilɪŋ əˈpɪrz pɔz brið ənd æsk wʌt ɪz ðɪs ˈfilɪŋ ˈtraɪɪŋ tu ʃoʊ mi/

segments.text: Is there a need under this feeling?
segments.ipa: /ɪz ðɛr ə nid ˈʌndər ðɪs ˈfilɪŋ/

segments.text: Is there a boundary I need?
segments.ipa: /ɪz ðɛr ə ˈbaʊndəri aɪ nid/

segments.text: Is there an old story I need to change?"
segments.ipa: /ɪz ðɛr æn oʊld ˈstɔri aɪ nid tu tʃeɪndʒ/

segments.text: You do not need to solve everything today.
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt nid tu sɑlv ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: Just listening to yourself is already a step up the mountain.
segments.ipa: /dʒʌst ˈlɪsənɪŋ tu jərˈsɛlf ɪz ɔlˈrɛdi ə stɛp ʌp ðə ˈmaʊntən/

segments.text: One of the most beautiful ideas in this book is the idea of becoming your future self.
segments.ipa: /wʌn ʌv ðə moʊst ˈbjutəfəl aɪˈdiəz ɪn ðɪs bʊk ɪz ðə aɪˈdiə ʌv bɪˈkʌmɪŋ jɔr ˈfjutʃər sɛlf/

segments.text: Your future self is the person you are becoming.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˈfjutʃər sɛlf ɪz ðə ˈpɝsən ju ɑr bɪˈkʌmɪŋ/

segments.text: It is the version of you who has grown.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ðə ˈvɝʒən ʌv ju hu hæz ɡroʊn/

segments.text: This person may be calmer, stronger, healthier, more confident, more disciplined, or more peaceful.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ˈpɝsən meɪ bi ˈkɑmər ˈstrɔŋər ˈhɛlθiər mɔr ˈkɑnfədənt mɔr ˈdɪsəplənd ɔr mɔr ˈpisfəl/

segments.text: This person is not a stranger.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ˈpɝsən ɪz nɑt ə ˈstreɪndʒər/

segments.text: This person is you.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ˈpɝsən ɪz ju/

segments.text: But, with new habits, new beliefs, and new choices.
segments.ipa: /bʌt wɪð nu ˈhæbəts nu bɪˈlifs ənd nu ˈtʃɔɪsəz/

segments.text: Many people wait for the future self to appear suddenly.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈpipəl weɪt fɔr ðə ˈfjutʃər sɛlf tu əˈpɪr ˈsʌdənli/

segments.text: They think, "One day, I will be confident.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ θɪŋk wʌn deɪ aɪ wɪl bi ˈkɑnfədənt/

segments.text: One day, I will be fluent.
segments.ipa: /wʌn deɪ aɪ wɪl bi ˈfluənt/

segments.text: One day, I will be organized.
segments.ipa: /wʌn deɪ aɪ wɪl bi ˈɔrɡəˌnaɪzd/

segments.text: One day, I will change."
segments.ipa: /wʌn deɪ aɪ wɪl tʃeɪndʒ/

segments.text: But, the future self does not arrive like magic.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðə ˈfjutʃər sɛlf dʌz nɑt ərˈaɪv laɪk ˈmædʒɪk/

segments.text: The future self is built by today's choices.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈfjutʃər sɛlf ɪz bɪlt baɪ təˈdeɪz ˈtʃɔɪsəz/

segments.text: This is very important.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈvɛri ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt/

segments.text: Your future is not only something that happens later.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˈfjutʃər ɪz nɑt ˈoʊnli ˈsʌmθɪŋ ðæt ˈhæpənz ˈleɪtər/

segments.text: Your future is something you practice now.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˈfjutʃər ɪz ˈsʌmθɪŋ ju ˈpræktəs naʊ/

segments.text: If you want to become a confident English speaker, what would that person do today?
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju wɑnt tu bɪˈkʌm ə ˈkɑnfədənt ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈspikər wʌt wʊd ðæt ˈpɝsən du təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: Maybe, they would practice speaking for 1 minute.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ wʊd ˈpræktəs ˈspikɪŋ fɔr ˈmɪnət/

segments.text: Maybe, they would listen to easy English.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ wʊd ˈlɪsən tu ˈizi ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: Maybe, they would listen to easy English.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ wʊd ˈlɪsən tu ˈizi ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: Maybe, they would repeat useful sentences.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ wʊd rɪˈpit ˈjusfəl ˈsɛntənsəz/

segments.text: Maybe, they would not attack themselves for mistakes.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ wʊd nɑt əˈtæk ðɛmˈsɛlvz fɔr mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: If you want to become healthier, what would that person do today?
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju wɑnt tu bɪˈkʌm ˈhɛlθiər wʌt wʊd ðæt ˈpɝsən du təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: Maybe, they would sleep earlier.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ wʊd slip ˈɝliər/

segments.text: Maybe, they would walk.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ wʊd wɔk/

segments.text: Maybe, they would drink water.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ wʊd drɪŋk ˈwɔtər/

segments.text: Maybe, they would eat in a way that gives energy.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ wʊd it ɪn ə weɪ ðæt ɡɪvz ˈɛnərdʒi/

segments.text: If you want to become peaceful, what would that person do today?
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju wɑnt tu bɪˈkʌm ˈpisfəl wʌt wʊd ðæt ˈpɝsən du təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: Maybe they would stop arguing with every thought.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ wʊd stɑp ˈɑrɡjuɪŋ wɪð ˈɛvəri θɔt/

segments.text: Maybe they would breathe.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ wʊd brið/

segments.text: Maybe they would say no to one unnecessary problem.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ wʊd seɪ noʊ tu wʌn ənˈnɛsəˌsɛri ˈprɑbləm/

segments.text: Maybe they would create a quiet morning routine.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðeɪ wʊd kriˈeɪt ə ˈkwaɪət ˈmɔrnɪŋ ruˈtin/

segments.text: The key question is simple.
segments.ipa: /ðə ki ˈkwɛstʃən ɪz ˈsɪmpəl/

segments.text: What would my future self choose now?
segments.ipa: /wʌt wʊd maɪ ˈfjutʃər sɛlf tʃuz naʊ/

segments.text: This question can guide you.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ˈkwɛstʃən kæn ɡaɪd ju/

segments.text: It makes change practical.
segments.ipa: /ɪt meɪks tʃeɪndʒ ˈpræktəkəl/

segments.text: You do not need to change your whole life in one day.
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt nid tu tʃeɪndʒ jɔr hoʊl laɪf ɪn wʌn deɪ/

segments.text: You just need to choose the next action from your future self, not from your old fear.
segments.ipa: /ju dʒʌst nid tu tʃuz ðə nɛkst ˈækʃən frʌm jɔr ˈfjutʃər sɛlf nɑt frʌm jɔr oʊld fɪr/

segments.text: The old self may say, "Avoid it."
segments.ipa: /ðə oʊld sɛlf meɪ seɪ əˈvɔɪd ɪt/

segments.text: The future self may say, "Try for 5 minutes."
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈfjutʃər sɛlf meɪ seɪ traɪ fɔr ˈmɪnəts/

segments.text: The old self may say, "You are not ready."
segments.ipa: /ðə oʊld sɛlf meɪ seɪ ju ɑr nɑt ˈrɛdi/

segments.text: The future self may say, "Start small."
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈfjutʃər sɛlf meɪ seɪ stɑrt smɔl/

segments.text: The old self may say, "This is too hard."
segments.ipa: /ðə oʊld sɛlf meɪ seɪ ðɪs ɪz tu hɑrd/

segments.text: The future self may say, "One step is enough."
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈfjutʃər sɛlf meɪ seɪ wʌn stɛp ɪz ɪˈnʌf/

segments.text: This is how identity changes.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz haʊ aɪˈdɛntɪˌti ˈtʃeɪndʒəz/

segments.text: Identity means the way you see yourself.
segments.ipa: /aɪˈdɛntɪˌti minz ðə weɪ ju si jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: If you see yourself as someone who always fails, your actions may follow that story.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju si jərˈsɛlf æz ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu ˈɔlˌweɪz feɪlz jɔr ˈækʃənz meɪ ˈfɑloʊ ðæt ˈstɔri/

segments.text: If you see yourself as someone who learns slowly but continues, your actions become different.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju si jərˈsɛlf æz ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu lɝnz ˈsloʊli bʌt kənˈtɪnjuz jɔr ˈækʃənz bɪˈkʌm ˈdɪfərənt/

segments.text: You do not need a fake identity.
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt nid ə feɪk aɪˈdɛntɪˌti/

segments.text: Do not say, "I am perfect."
segments.ipa: /du nɑt seɪ aɪ æm pərˈfɛkt/

segments.text: That is not true.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz nɑt tru/

segments.text: Say something real and helpful.
segments.ipa: /seɪ ˈsʌmθɪŋ ril ənd ˈhɛlpfəl/

segments.text: I am someone who practices.
segments.ipa: /aɪ æm ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu ˈpræktəsəz/

segments.text: I am someone who keeps going.
segments.ipa: /aɪ æm ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu kips ˈɡoʊɪŋ/

segments.text: I am someone who can learn.
segments.ipa: /aɪ æm ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu kæn lɝn/

segments.text: I am someone who can change.
segments.ipa: /aɪ æm ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu kæn tʃeɪndʒ/

segments.text: These sentences are simple, but they slowly shape your mind.
segments.ipa: /ðiz ˈsɛntənsəz ɑr ˈsɪmpəl bʌt ðeɪ ˈsloʊli ʃeɪp jɔr maɪnd/

segments.text: The book teaches that we often stay stuck because we are loyal to an old version of ourselves.
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk ˈtitʃəz ðæt wi ˈɔfən steɪ stʌk bɪˈkɔz wi ɑr ˈlɔɪəl tu æn oʊld ˈvɝʒən ʌv aʊərˈsɛlvz/

segments.text: We are faithful.
segments.ipa: /wi ɑr ˈfeɪθfəl/

segments.text: We keep protecting the old identity.
segments.ipa: /wi kip prəˈtɛktɪŋ ðə oʊld aɪˈdɛntɪˌti/

segments.text: Maybe the old identity says, "I am shy."
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðə oʊld aɪˈdɛntɪˌti sɛz aɪ æm ʃaɪ/

segments.text: Or, "I am bad at languages."
segments.ipa: /ɔr aɪ æm bæd æt ˈlæŋɡwədʒəz/

segments.text: Or, "I never finish things."
segments.ipa: /ɔr aɪ ˈnɛvər ˈfɪnɪʃ θɪŋz/

segments.text: Or, "I cannot handle success."
segments.ipa: /ɔr aɪ ˈkænɑt ˈhændəl səkˈsɛs/

segments.text: These stories may feel familiar, but they may not be true anymore.
segments.ipa: /ðiz ˈstɔriz meɪ fil fəˈmɪljər bʌt ðeɪ meɪ nɑt bi tru ˌɛniˈmɔr/

segments.text: Sometimes, growth means letting an old identity die.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz ɡroʊθ minz ˈlɛtɪŋ æn oʊld aɪˈdɛntɪˌti daɪ/

segments.text: Not your real self, only the old story.
segments.ipa: /nɑt jɔr ril sɛlf ˈoʊnli ðə oʊld ˈstɔri/

segments.text: This can feel strange.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs kæn fil streɪndʒ/

segments.text: Even positive change can feel like loss.
segments.ipa: /ˈivɪn ˈpɑzətɪv tʃeɪndʒ kæn fil laɪk lɔs/

segments.text: If you become more confident, some old relationships may change.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju bɪˈkʌm mɔr ˈkɑnfədənt sʌm oʊld riˈleɪʃənˌʃɪps meɪ tʃeɪndʒ/

segments.text: If you become more disciplined, some old habits may disappear.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju bɪˈkʌm mɔr ˈdɪsəplənd sʌm oʊld ˈhæbəts meɪ ˌdɪsəˈpɪr/

segments.text: If you become calmer, drama may no longer feel exciting.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju bɪˈkʌm ˈkɑmər ˈdrɑmə meɪ noʊ ˈlɔŋɡər fil ɪkˈsaɪtɪŋ/

segments.text: If you become successful, you may not recognize your old life.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju bɪˈkʌm səkˈsɛsfəl ju meɪ nɑt ˈrɛkəɡˌnaɪz jɔr oʊld laɪf/

segments.text: So, part of you may resist change.
segments.ipa: /soʊ pɑrt ʌv ju meɪ rɪˈzɪst tʃeɪndʒ/

segments.text: Resist means push against.
segments.ipa: /rɪˈzɪst minz pʊʃ əˈɡɛnst/

segments.text: You may say, "I want this."
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ seɪ aɪ wɑnt ðɪs/

segments.text: But another part says, "This is unfamiliar."
segments.ipa: /bʌt əˈnʌðər pɑrt sɛz ðɪs ɪz ˌʌnfəˈmɪljər/

segments.text: This is why we need patience.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz waɪ wi nid ˈpeɪʃəns/

segments.text: You are not only building new habits, you are teaching your mind and body that a new life is safe.
segments.ipa: /ju ɑr nɑt ˈoʊnli ˈbɪldɪŋ nu ˈhæbəts ju ɑr ˈtitʃɪŋ jɔr maɪnd ənd ˈbɑdi ðæt ə nu laɪf ɪz seɪf/

segments.text: For English learners, maybe your old identity is, "I am not good at speaking."
segments.ipa: /fɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnərz ˈmeɪbi jɔr oʊld aɪˈdɛntɪˌti ɪz aɪ æm nɑt ɡʊd æt ˈspikɪŋ/

segments.text: But you can build a new identity.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ju kæn bɪld ə nu aɪˈdɛntɪˌti/

segments.text: "I am becoming someone who speaks English every day."
segments.ipa: /aɪ æm bɪˈkʌmɪŋ ˈsʌmˌwʌn hu spiks ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈɛvəri deɪ/

segments.text: Notice the word becoming.
segments.ipa: /ˈnoʊtəs ðə wɝd bɪˈkʌmɪŋ/

segments.text: It is gentle.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ˈdʒɛntəl/

segments.text: It allows process.
segments.ipa: /ɪt əˈlaʊz ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: You do not have to say, "I am fluent today."
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt hæv tu seɪ aɪ æm ˈfluənt təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: You can say, "I am becoming more fluent."
segments.ipa: /ju kæn seɪ aɪ æm bɪˈkʌmɪŋ mɔr ˈfluənt/

segments.text: Becoming is a beautiful word.
segments.ipa: /bɪˈkʌmɪŋ ɪz ə ˈbjutəfəl wɝd/

segments.text: It means you are in progress.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz ju ɑr ɪn ˈprɑˌɡrɛs/

segments.text: You are not finished.
segments.ipa: /ju ɑr nɑt ˈfɪnɪʃt/

segments.text: You are growing.
segments.ipa: /ju ɑr ˈɡroʊɪŋ/

segments.text: Your future self is created by repetition.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˈfjutʃər sɛlf ɪz kriˈeɪtəd baɪ ˌrɛpəˈtɪʃən/

segments.text: If you repeat fear, fear becomes stronger.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju rɪˈpit fɪr fɪr bɪˈkʌmz ˈstrɔŋər/

segments.text: If you repeat avoidance, avoidance becomes stronger.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju rɪˈpit əˈvɔɪdəns əˈvɔɪdəns bɪˈkʌmz ˈstrɔŋər/

segments.text: If you repeat practice, practice becomes natural.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju rɪˈpit ˈpræktəs ˈpræktəs bɪˈkʌmz ˈnætʃərəl/

segments.text: If you repeat calm choices, calm becomes easier.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju rɪˈpit kɑm ˈtʃɔɪsəz kɑm bɪˈkʌmz ˈiziər/

segments.text: This is why daily habits matter.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz waɪ ˈdeɪli ˈhæbəts ˈmætər/

segments.text: A habit is a vote for your future self.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈhæbət ɪz ə voʊt fɔr jɔr ˈfjutʃər sɛlf/

segments.text: Every time you practice, you say, "This is who I am becoming."
segments.ipa: /ˈɛvəri taɪm ju ˈpræktəs ju seɪ ðɪs ɪz hu aɪ æm bɪˈkʌmɪŋ/

segments.text: Every time you keep a promise to yourself, you build trust with yourself.
segments.ipa: /ˈɛvəri taɪm ju kip ə ˈprɑməs tu jərˈsɛlf ju bɪld trʌst wɪð jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: And self-trust is powerful.
segments.ipa: /ənd self-trust ɪz ˈpaʊərfəl/

segments.text: It means you believe your own words.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz ju bɪˈliv jɔr oʊn wɝdz/

segments.text: Many people lose self-trust because they often break promises to themselves.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈpipəl luz self-trust bɪˈkɔz ðeɪ ˈɔfən breɪk ˈprɑməsəz tu ðɛmˈsɛlvz/

segments.text: They say, "Tomorrow I will start."
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ seɪ təˈmɑˌroʊ aɪ wɪl stɑrt/

segments.text: But they do not start.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðeɪ du nɑt stɑrt/

segments.text: They say, "I will practice every day."
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ seɪ aɪ wɪl ˈpræktəs ˈɛvəri deɪ/

segments.text: But they stop after 2 days.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðeɪ stɑp ˈæftər deɪz/

segments.text: Then they feel disappointed.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ðeɪ fil ˌdɪsəˈpɔɪntɪd/

segments.text: But you can rebuild self-trust with very small promises.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ju kæn riˈbɪld self-trust wɪð ˈvɛri smɔl ˈprɑməsəz/

segments.text: Do not promise too much.
segments.ipa: /du nɑt ˈprɑməs tu mʌtʃ/

segments.text: Promise something small and keep it.
segments.ipa: /ˈprɑməs ˈsʌmθɪŋ smɔl ənd kip ɪt/

segments.text: Say, "I will listen to English for 5 minutes."
segments.ipa: /seɪ aɪ wɪl ˈlɪsən tu ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ fɔr ˈmɪnəts/

segments.text: Then do it.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn du ɪt/

segments.text: Say, "I will write three sentences."
segments.ipa: /seɪ aɪ wɪl raɪt θri ˈsɛntənsəz/

segments.text: Then do it.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn du ɪt/

segments.text: Say, "I will speak for 1 minute."
segments.ipa: /seɪ aɪ wɪl spik fɔr ˈmɪnət/

segments.text: Then do it.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn du ɪt/

segments.text: Small promises kept are better than big promises broken.
segments.ipa: /smɔl ˈprɑməsəz kɛpt ɑr ˈbɛtər ðæn bɪɡ ˈprɑməsəz ˈbroʊkən/

segments.text: The future self is not built by one huge action.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈfjutʃər sɛlf ɪz nɑt bɪlt baɪ wʌn hjudʒ ˈækʃən/

segments.text: It is built by many small actions that match the person you want to become.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz bɪlt baɪ ˈmɛni smɔl ˈækʃənz ðæt mætʃ ðə ˈpɝsən ju wɑnt tu bɪˈkʌm/

segments.text: So, ask yourself today, "Who am I becoming?
segments.ipa: /soʊ æsk jərˈsɛlf təˈdeɪ hu æm aɪ bɪˈkʌmɪŋ/

segments.text: What is one small action that matches that person?
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɪz wʌn smɔl ˈækʃən ðæt ˈmætʃəz ðæt ˈpɝsən/

segments.text: What would my future self thank me for?
segments.ipa: /wʌt wʊd maɪ ˈfjutʃər sɛlf θæŋk mi fɔr/

segments.text: You do not need to climb the whole mountain today.
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt nid tu klaɪm ðə hoʊl ˈmaʊntən təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: Just take the next step as the person you are becoming." All right.
segments.ipa: /dʒʌst teɪk ðə nɛkst stɛp æz ðə ˈpɝsən ju ɑr bɪˈkʌmɪŋ ɔl raɪt/

segments.text: Another deep idea in this book is that we cannot fully move forward if we are still controlled by the past.
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər dip aɪˈdiə ɪn ðɪs bʊk ɪz ðæt wi ˈkænɑt ˈfʊli muv ˈfɔrwərd ɪf wi ɑr stɪl kənˈtroʊld baɪ ðə pæst/

segments.text: The past is not only what happened before.
segments.ipa: /ðə pæst ɪz nɑt ˈoʊnli wʌt ˈhæpənd bɪˈfɔr/

segments.text: The past can live inside our thoughts, our emotions, our habits, and our reactions.
segments.ipa: /ðə pæst kæn laɪv ˌɪnˈsaɪd ˈaʊər θɔts ˈaʊər ɪˈmoʊʃənz ˈaʊər ˈhæbəts ənd ˈaʊər riˈækʃənz/

segments.text: Sometimes something happened years ago, but our body still reacts as if it is happening now.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz ˈsʌmθɪŋ ˈhæpənd jɪrz əˈɡoʊ bʌt ˈaʊər ˈbɑdi stɪl riˈækts æz ɪf ɪt ɪz ˈhæpənɪŋ naʊ/

segments.text: A small comment can make us feel rejected.
segments.ipa: /ə smɔl ˈkɑmɛnt kæn meɪk ʌs fil rɪˈdʒɛktɪd/

segments.text: A mistake can make us feel ashamed.
segments.ipa: /ə mɪˈsteɪk kæn meɪk ʌs fil əˈʃeɪmd/

segments.text: A difficult conversation can make us feel unsafe.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈdɪfəkəlt ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃən kæn meɪk ʌs fil ənˈseɪf/

segments.text: This is why healing matters.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz waɪ ˈhilɪŋ ˈmætərz/

segments.text: Healing does not Healing does not mean pretending the past was fine.
segments.ipa: /ˈhilɪŋ dʌz nɑt ˈhilɪŋ dʌz nɑt min priˈtɛndɪŋ ðə pæst wɑz faɪn/

segments.text: Healing does not mean saying pain was okay.
segments.ipa: /ˈhilɪŋ dʌz nɑt min ˈseɪɪŋ peɪn wɑz ˌoʊˈkeɪ/

segments.text: Healing means the past no longer controls your whole life.
segments.ipa: /ˈhilɪŋ minz ðə pæst noʊ ˈlɔŋɡər kənˈtroʊlz jɔr hoʊl laɪf/

segments.text: You can remember something without living inside it every day.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn rɪˈmɛmbər ˈsʌmθɪŋ wɪˈθaʊt ˈlɪvɪŋ ˌɪnˈsaɪd ɪt ˈɛvəri deɪ/

segments.text: This is not easy, but it is possible.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz nɑt ˈizi bʌt ɪt ɪz ˈpɑsəbəl/

segments.text: The book teaches that many of our patterns come from old pain.
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk ˈtitʃəz ðæt ˈmɛni ʌv ˈaʊər ˈpætərnz kʌm frʌm oʊld peɪn/

segments.text: Maybe you learned to protect yourself by becoming silent.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju lɝnd tu prəˈtɛkt jərˈsɛlf baɪ bɪˈkʌmɪŋ ˈsaɪlənt/

segments.text: Maybe you learned to please everyone because you were afraid of conflict.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju lɝnd tu pliz ˈɛvriˌwʌn bɪˈkɔz ju wɝ əˈfreɪd ʌv ˈkɑnflɪkt/

segments.text: Maybe you learned to work too much because you wanted approval.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju lɝnd tu wɝk tu mʌtʃ bɪˈkɔz ju ˈwɔntɪd əˈpruvəl/

segments.text: Maybe you learned to avoid risks because failure felt dangerous.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju lɝnd tu əˈvɔɪd rɪsks bɪˈkɔz ˈfeɪljər fɛlt ˈdeɪndʒərəs/

segments.text: At one time, these patterns may have helped you survive.
segments.ipa: /æt wʌn taɪm ðiz ˈpætərnz meɪ hæv hɛlpt ju sərˈvaɪv/

segments.text: They may have protected you.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ meɪ hæv prəˈtɛktɪd ju/

segments.text: But now, they may be stopping you.
segments.ipa: /bʌt naʊ ðeɪ meɪ bi ˈstɑpɪŋ ju/

segments.text: This is an important sentence.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz æn ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: What protected you in the past may be limiting you now.
segments.ipa: /wʌt prəˈtɛktɪd ju ɪn ðə pæst meɪ bi ˈlɪmətɪŋ ju naʊ/

segments.text: For example, maybe staying quiet protected you when people were critical.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ˈmeɪbi ˈsteɪɪŋ ˈkwaɪət prəˈtɛktɪd ju wɛn ˈpipəl wɝ ˈkrɪtɪkəl/

segments.text: But now, staying quiet stops you from sharing your ideas.
segments.ipa: /bʌt naʊ ˈsteɪɪŋ ˈkwaɪət stɑps ju frʌm ˈʃɛrɪŋ jɔr aɪˈdiəz/

segments.text: Maybe pleasing everyone protected you from rejection.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ˈplizɪŋ ˈɛvriˌwʌn prəˈtɛktɪd ju frʌm rɪˈdʒɛkʃən/

segments.text: But now pleasing everyone makes you tired.
segments.ipa: /bʌt naʊ ˈplizɪŋ ˈɛvriˌwʌn meɪks ju ˈtaɪərd/

segments.text: Maybe avoiding risks protected you from embarrassment.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi əˈvɔɪdɪŋ rɪsks prəˈtɛktɪd ju frʌm ɪmˈbɛrəsmənt/

segments.text: But now avoiding risks stops your growth.
segments.ipa: /bʌt naʊ əˈvɔɪdɪŋ rɪsks stɑps jɔr ɡroʊθ/

segments.text: So healing begins when we understand the old pattern with kindness.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ˈhilɪŋ bɪˈɡɪnz wɛn wi ˌʌndərˈstænd ðə oʊld ˈpætərn wɪð ˈkaɪndnəs/

segments.text: We do not say, "I was stupid."
segments.ipa: /wi du nɑt seɪ aɪ wɑz ˈstupəd/

segments.text: We say, "I learned this pattern for a reason.
segments.ipa: /wi seɪ aɪ lɝnd ðɪs ˈpætərn fɔr ə ˈrizən/

segments.text: But maybe I do not need it anymore."
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈmeɪbi aɪ du nɑt nid ɪt ˌɛniˈmɔr/

segments.text: This is a gentle way to change.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ə ˈdʒɛntəl weɪ tu tʃeɪndʒ/

segments.text: For English learners, maybe you had a bad experience in school.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnərz ˈmeɪbi ju hæd ə bæd ɪkˈspɪriəns ɪn skul/

segments.text: Maybe a teacher corrected you harshly.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ə ˈtitʃər kərˈɛktəd ju ˈhɑrʃli/

segments.text: Maybe classmates laughed at your pronunciation.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ˈklæˌsmeɪts læft æt jɔr proʊˌnʌnsiˈeɪʃən/

segments.text: Maybe you felt embarrassed when speaking.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju fɛlt ɪmˈbɛrəst wɛn ˈspikɪŋ/

segments.text: Now years later, you still feel fear when you try to speak English.
segments.ipa: /naʊ jɪrz ˈleɪtər ju stɪl fil fɪr wɛn ju traɪ tu spik ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: The old moment is gone.
segments.ipa: /ðə oʊld ˈmoʊmənt ɪz ɡɔn/

segments.text: But the feeling remains.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðə ˈfilɪŋ rɪˈmeɪnz/

segments.text: Healing means telling yourself a new truth.
segments.ipa: /ˈhilɪŋ minz ˈtɛlɪŋ jərˈsɛlf ə nu truθ/

segments.text: That was then.
segments.ipa: /ðæt wɑz ðɛn/

segments.text: This is now.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz naʊ/

segments.text: I am safe to learn.
segments.ipa: /aɪ æm seɪf tu lɝn/

segments.text: I am allowed to make mistakes.
segments.ipa: /aɪ æm əˈlaʊd tu meɪk mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: This sentence can be powerful.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ˈsɛntəns kæn bi ˈpaʊərfəl/

segments.text: I am allowed to make mistakes.
segments.ipa: /aɪ æm əˈlaʊd tu meɪk mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: Language learning needs mistakes.
segments.ipa: /ˈlæŋɡwədʒ ˈlɝnɪŋ nidz mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: You cannot learn without them.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈkænɑt lɝn wɪˈθaʊt ðɛm/

segments.text: Every mistake is not a sign of failure.
segments.ipa: /ˈɛvəri mɪˈsteɪk ɪz nɑt ə saɪn ʌv ˈfeɪljər/

segments.text: It is a sign that you are using the language.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ə saɪn ðæt ju ɑr ˈjuzɪŋ ðə ˈlæŋɡwədʒ/

segments.text: And when you use the language, you grow.
segments.ipa: /ənd wɛn ju jus ðə ˈlæŋɡwədʒ ju ɡroʊ/

segments.text: The book also shows that healing is connected to responsibility.
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk ˈɔlsoʊ ʃoʊz ðæt ˈhilɪŋ ɪz kəˈnɛktɪd tu riˌspɑnsəˈbɪləti/

segments.text: Responsibility does not mean blame.
segments.ipa: /riˌspɑnsəˈbɪləti dʌz nɑt min bleɪm/

segments.text: It means the ability to respond.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz ðə əˈbɪləˌti tu rɪˈspɑnd/

segments.text: Maybe you did not choose what hurt you.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju dɪd nɑt tʃuz wʌt hɝt ju/

segments.text: Maybe you did not choose the difficult situation, but now, as an adult, you can choose how to respond.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju dɪd nɑt tʃuz ðə ˈdɪfəkəlt ˌsɪtʃuˈeɪʃən bʌt naʊ æz æn əˈdʌlt ju kæn tʃuz haʊ tu rɪˈspɑnd/

segments.text: You can choose healing.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn tʃuz ˈhilɪŋ/

segments.text: You can choose support.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn tʃuz səˈpɔrt/

segments.text: You can choose better habits.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn tʃuz ˈbɛtər ˈhæbəts/

segments.text: You can choose not to repeat the same pattern forever.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn tʃuz nɑt tu rɪˈpit ðə seɪm ˈpætərn fərˈɛvər/

segments.text: This is not always fair.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz nɑt ˈɔlˌweɪz fɛr/

segments.text: Sometimes we have to heal from things we did not create, but healing gives us freedom.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz wi hæv tu hil frʌm θɪŋz wi dɪd nɑt kriˈeɪt bʌt ˈhilɪŋ ɡɪvz ʌs ˈfridəm/

segments.text: It says, "I will not let this pain control my whole future."
segments.ipa: /ɪt sɛz aɪ wɪl nɑt lɛt ðɪs peɪn kənˈtroʊl maɪ hoʊl ˈfjutʃər/

segments.text: Another part of healing is grief.
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər pɑrt ʌv ˈhilɪŋ ɪz ɡrif/

segments.text: Grief is the sadness we feel when we lose something.
segments.ipa: /ɡrif ɪz ðə ˈsædnəs wi fil wɛn wi luz ˈsʌmθɪŋ/

segments.text: We may grieve a person, a relationship, a dream, a childhood, an old identity,
segments.ipa: /wi meɪ ɡriv ə ˈpɝsən ə riˈleɪʃənˌʃɪp ə drim ə ˈtʃaɪldˌhʊd æn oʊld aɪˈdɛntɪˌti/

segments.text: or a life we wanted but did not have.
segments.ipa: /ɔr ə laɪf wi ˈwɔntɪd bʌt dɪd nɑt hæv/

segments.text: Many people do not allow themselves to grieve.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈpipəl du nɑt əˈlaʊ ðɛmˈsɛlvz tu ɡriv/

segments.text: They say, "It is fine."
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ seɪ ɪt ɪz faɪn/

segments.text: They say, "I should be over it."
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ seɪ aɪ ʃʊd bi ˈoʊvər ɪt/

segments.text: They say, "Other people have worse problems."
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ seɪ ˈʌðər ˈpipəl hæv wɝs ˈprɑbləmz/

segments.text: But feelings do not disappear because we compare them.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈfilɪŋz du nɑt ˌdɪsəˈpɪr bɪˈkɔz wi kəmˈpɛr ðɛm/

segments.text: Your pain matters because it is yours.
segments.ipa: /jɔr peɪn ˈmætərz bɪˈkɔz ɪt ɪz jʊrz/

segments.text: Grieving is not weakness.
segments.ipa: /ˈɡrivɪŋ ɪz nɑt ˈwiknəs/

segments.text: It is part of letting go.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz pɑrt ʌv ˈlɛtɪŋ ɡoʊ/

segments.text: When you allow yourself to feel sadness, the sadness can move through you.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju əˈlaʊ jərˈsɛlf tu fil ˈsædnəs ðə ˈsædnəs kæn muv θru ju/

segments.text: When you keep it inside forever, it can become heavy.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju kip ɪt ˌɪnˈsaɪd fərˈɛvər ɪt kæn bɪˈkʌm ˈhɛvi/

segments.text: Letting go does not happen by force.
segments.ipa: /ˈlɛtɪŋ ɡoʊ dʌz nɑt ˈhæpən baɪ fɔrs/

segments.text: You cannot simply say "I let go and finish everything."
segments.ipa: /ju ˈkænɑt ˈsɪmpli seɪ aɪ lɛt ɡoʊ ənd ˈfɪnɪʃ ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ/

segments.text: Letting go often happens slowly. You understand. You feel.
segments.ipa: /ˈlɛtɪŋ ɡoʊ ˈɔfən ˈhæpənz ˈsloʊli ju ˌʌndərˈstænd ju fil/

segments.text: You cry, maybe.
segments.ipa: /ju kraɪ ˈmeɪbi/

segments.text: You speak to someone. You write. You rest.
segments.ipa: /ju spik tu ˈsʌmˌwʌn ju raɪt ju rɛst/

segments.text: You choose new actions.
segments.ipa: /ju tʃuz nu ˈækʃənz/

segments.text: Then, little by little, the past becomes less heavy.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ˈlɪtəl baɪ ˈlɪtəl ðə pæst bɪˈkʌmz lɛs ˈhɛvi/

segments.text: The book encourages us to stop waiting for closure from other people.
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk ɛnˈkɝɪdʒɪz ʌs tu stɑp ˈweɪtɪŋ fɔr ˈkloʊʒər frʌm ˈʌðər ˈpipəl/

segments.text: Closure means a feeling that something is finished and understood.
segments.ipa: /ˈkloʊʒər minz ə ˈfilɪŋ ðæt ˈsʌmθɪŋ ɪz ˈfɪnɪʃt ənd ˌʌndərˈstʊd/

segments.text: Sometimes, we want someone to explain.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz wi wɑnt ˈsʌmˌwʌn tu ɪkˈspleɪn/

segments.text: Sometimes, we want someone to admit that they hurt us.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz wi wɑnt ˈsʌmˌwʌn tu ədˈmɪt ðæt ðeɪ hɝt ʌs/

segments.text: But, we may never get that.
segments.ipa: /bʌt wi meɪ ˈnɛvər ɡɛt ðæt/

segments.text: If our peace depends on another person changing, we may wait forever.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ˈaʊər pis dɪˈpɛndz ɑn əˈnʌðər ˈpɝsən ˈtʃeɪndʒɪŋ wi meɪ weɪt fərˈɛvər/

segments.text: So, we need to create our own closure.
segments.ipa: /soʊ wi nid tu kriˈeɪt ˈaʊər oʊn ˈkloʊʒər/

segments.text: This is not easy, but it is powerful. Okay.
